walkthroughs.body_html:
Tropical storms need 4 conditions:

1. Warm ocean (≥27°C, 50m deep)
2. Latitude 5°-30° (Coriolis spin)
3. Low wind shear (calm upper air)
4. Atmospheric instability

No storms form on the Equator (no Coriolis).

Step by step:

1. Warm sea evaporates water
2. Air rises, cools, condenses → releases latent heat
3. More air sucked in → spins via Coriolis effect
4. Eye forms at calm centre

The storm feeds on warm water.

How will warming affect storms?

• Stronger storms (warmer seas = more energy)
• Higher storm surges (sea-level rise)
• More rainfall (warmer air = more moisture)
• Frequency may not change much

Likely more intense, not more frequent.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.

options: Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
